summary: Karunapati Tripathi was an Indology scholar who served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan. He also taught Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi.

Karunesh Shukla, an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied under V. P. Upadhyaya and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation. He served as Reader (attested 1973) and Professor and Head of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages (attested 1991) at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz earned her PhD (1991) and Habilitation (1999) from the University of Bonn. Specializing in Tibetology, religious studies, and Central Asian studies, she became Professor (1999), Dean of the Philosophisch-historischen Fakultät (2007–2010), and Emerita (around 2024) at the University of Bern.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (MA, around 1906–1909), and Lincoln's Inn. Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he was Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta in 1917 and served as president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit worked in Indology and archaeology, holding posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and serving as Officiating Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1931). From 1937 to 1944, he was Deputy Director-General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India.

Indologist Kashinath Trimbak Telang earned an MA and LLB from Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (around 1864–1872). He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone, President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (around 1915–1945). He was later an Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957) and taught Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla and Masaaki Hattori.

Kasten Anders Rönnow, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Jarl Charpentier at Uppsala University (Fil.kand., around 1915–1918). He later served as Acting Professor at Uppsala University (1928) and at Lund University (1932–1933).

Katarzyna Marciniak is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar based at the University of Warsaw, where she served as a Postdoctorate Researcher in the Research Centre of Buddhist Studies (attested 2016) and as an adjunct (2020).

Kate Crosby, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned her BA and DPhil from the University of Oxford and studied at Hamburg and Kelaniya. She held posts at SOAS and King's College London before becoming Professor of Buddhist Studies at Oxford in 2022.

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London in 2008. She was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.

Katharina Sabernig is a Tibetology scholar who completed an MD at the Medical University of Vienna (1997–2008) and a PhD at the University of Vienna (2007–2017). She holds a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katharine von Garnier-Moewes was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the University of Leipzig and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University in 1907.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar of Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Indology. She completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann and was also taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA from the University of Chicago and a PhD from McGill University (around 1970–1977). She served as a professor at McGill University from around 1978 to 2017.

Kathleen D. Morrison studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1987–1992). An archaeologist and Indologist, she served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern University (around 1994–1996) and became Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2017.

Kathleen Gough, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned her PhD from Girton College, Cambridge (1943–1950). She held posts at Brandeis (1961–1963), Oregon (1963–1967), and Simon Fraser (1967–1970), before becoming an Honorary Research Associate at British Columbia in 1970.

Kathleen Higgins is a philosophy scholar who earned her PhD from Yale University. She became a professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 1992 and held visiting appointments at the Bellagio Center, Australian National University, and Canberra School of Music.
